initial.logo: Use case: logo-brand. Asset type: transparent PNG wordmark for the original tactical FPS video game COLD ENTRY, usable on a dark main menu, loading screen, and cover. Design one finished premium wordmark, not a sheet of variations or a mockup. Exact text: "COLD ENTRY". Heavy custom condensed industrial sans-serif lettering, refined proportions and generous precise spacing, restrained military wayfinding character. Two lines COLD above ENTRY, aligned as one compact rectangular title lockup, all letters fully readable at small scale. Warm ivory lettering with a small restrained oxidized-orange vertical threshold/slit detail integrated into the E in ENTRY, suggest a breached doorway through negative space. Sophisticated understated surface wear confined to letter interiors, strong clean outer silhouettes; flat design, no 3D extrusion or glow. The game's setting is an abandoned industrial security facility deep in a cold conifer forest. No skulls, crosshairs, weapons, soldiers, flags, existing game emblems, slogans, or extra text. Center the complete isolated logo with comfortable transparent padding. True transparent background, no backdrop, no checkerboard drawn into the image.
initial.background: Use case: ads-marketing. Asset type: cinematic key art / widescreen main-menu and loading-screen background for the original tactical FPS COLD ENTRY. Create a finished AAA-quality photorealistic game illustration, landscape 16:9 composition (ideally 3840x2160). Composition: restrained environmental storytelling, human eye height from a dark wooded verge, the facility framed by trees in the middle distance; on the right foreground a single original tactical operator seen from behind/three-quarter back in generic olive and charcoal protective gear, holding a carbine low and cautiously observing the annex. Avoid overdone teal/orange grading, explosions, zombies, sci-fi gear, flags, real brand logos, existing game branding, game HUD, artificial borders. No typography, no text, no watermark. This is promotional concept/key art, not a screenshot.
